subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Forty Days of Mourning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Forty Days of Mourning.

hook.text: Ancient Egyptians mummified bodies over forty days. The dead needed forty days to prepare for the afterlife.

buildup.text: In many cultures, mourning lasts forty days. Greek, Armenian, and Filipino traditions observe this period.

discovery.text: The forty-day mourning period lets grief transform. Day one and day forty produce different kinds of sorrow.

twist.text: Lent lasts forty days—a communal mourning period before Easter's resurrection. The calendar encodes grief.

climax.text: Forty days is the universal timer for emotional transformation. Long enough to change you, short enough to end.

punchline.text: Grief takes forty days. Then you're different.

quiz.question: How long does the Christian observance of Lent last?
